look_here_first: Look for opposite long-petioled broad leaves with coarse teeth and three strong basal veins, topped by loose white flat-topped clusters of tiny all-disk heads—no ray florets.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: erect rhizomatous perennial of shaded/moist sites; opposite broadly ovate to triangular long-petioled leaves; leaves coarsely toothed with three strong veins from near base; terminal corymbiform clusters of many small white heads; heads discoid: white disk florets only, no rays

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Broadly ovate/triangular, coarsely toothed, commonly 3-veined from near base.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: White discoid heads with no ray florets.

key_traits.label: Reproductive confirmation
key_traits.text: Mature cypselae glabrous, not hispid, contrasted with A. havanensis (Flora of North America).

lookalikes.differences: FNA: A. altissima is herbaceous, with larger usually long-petioled, coarsely double-toothed leaves and GLABROUS cypselae; A. havanensis has a persistent woody shrub framework, shorter-petioled generally smaller leaves, and HISPID cypselae. Chromolaena odorata shows much longer cylindrical involucres (8–10 mm) with 4–6+ phyllary series.
